title: What the Rain Keeps
poem: i.  A photograph insists: this happened, this was warm.
ii.  I have a memory of the sea I cannot have earned.
iii.  I keep an inventory of tendernesses meant for someone else.
iv.  Each morning I assemble the same face and hope it holds till dark.
v.  I counted my breaths to be sure they were mine. The number changes.
colophon: drift and pull; a field that never settles the same way twice.
